messages.text: USA's Novak builds six-shot lead after three rounds at Mexico Open

metadata.summary: Andrew Novak built a comfortable lead at the turn and then poured it on by going five under par on the first five holes of the back nine on his way to a nine-under 62 as he built a six-shot lead at the Mexico Open.
metadata.content: Mexico Open: Andrew Novak builds six-shot lead after three rounds at PGA Tour event following stellar Saturday display | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mexico Open: Andrew Novak builds six-shot lead after three rounds at PGA Tour event following stellar Saturday display Saturday's third round of the Mexico Open sees the USA's Andrew Novak build six-shot lead at PGA Tour event; France's Matthieu Pavon currently sits second in standings; watch live coverage of the final round of the Mexico Open from 8pm on Sky Sports Golf on Sunday Sunday 1 November 2026 00:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the third round of the Mexico Open Andrew Novak built a comfortable lead at the turn and then poured it on by going five under par on the first five holes of the back nine on his way to a nine-under 62 as he built a six-shot lead at the Mexico Open. About the only thing Novak did wrong at Vidanta Vallarta was losing the handle on a club twirl at the par-five 12th while admiring a 279-yard shot that settled 20 feet away for an eagle. That was part of his sublime stretch of three birdies and an eagle that extended his lead to seven shots. It was such a great day for Novak that even when he had a lie in the rough with a golf ball well below his feet, he hammered that out to six feet on the 14th for a birdie. messages.text: Hamilton: A dream to emulate Schumacher with first Ferrari pole

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton said he had achieved his "dream" of emulating Michael Schumacher after claiming his first pole position for Ferrari at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton says it's a 'dream' to emulate Michael Schumacher after claiming his first Ferrari pole at the Mexico City GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Lewis Hamilton says it's a 'dream' to emulate Michael Schumacher after claiming his first Ferrari pole at the Mexico City GP Lewis Hamilton became F1's oldest pole-sitter in 44 years after claiming his first Ferrari pole at the Mexico City Grand Prix; the result secured a record-extending 105th career pole for the Brit; watch Sunday's race at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1 Sunday 1 November 2026 07:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton joins Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok to look back on his first pole position for Ferrari at the Mexico City GP Lewis Hamilton said he had achieved his "dream" of emulating Michael Schumacher after claiming his first pole position for Ferrari at the Mexico City Grand Prix. The 41-year-old unexpectedly snatched pole from Mercedes' George Russell in a thrilling end to qualifying to take his first pole in over three years and extend his record career pole tally to 105. Hamilton and Schumacher share the sport's record for the most Drivers' Championships with seven each, but while the Brit won one title with McLaren and the other six with Mercedes, the bulk of Schumacher's success came at Ferrari as he won five in a row from 2000 to 2004. metadata.content: London City Lionesses: Eder Maestre explains how his team are succeeding in the WSL ahead of big Man City test | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive London City Lionesses: Eder Maestre explains how his team are succeeding in the WSL ahead of big Man City test Watch London City Lionesses vs Man City in the WSL on Sunday, live on Sky Sports; kick-off 12pm; watch in-game clips and free match highlights across Sky Sports' digital platforms; buy tickets for the game by searching for the London City Lionesses website Charlotte Marsh Senior Football Journalist Sunday 1 November 2026 08:02, UK The sight of superstars rolling into London City Lionesses this summer was exciting for many, but there was one man who was tasked with making them a team - head coach Eder Maestre. Some questioned how he was going to balance a team of such talent - both incoming and already present - most of whom are used to starting, along with Michele Kang's vision for disruption - smash the traditional big three and qualify for Europe. And it is so far, so good. The Bromley-based club are third in the WSL with 16 points - already seven ahead of Arsenal - and have proven their summer acquisitions were more than just big names through the door. Nicolas Jackson scored his eighth goal in 10 games but an error from goalkeeper Zion Suzuki meant Aston Villa had to settle for a 1-1 draw at home to Fulham. Villa should have gone ahead after 15 minutes when they were awarded a penalty following a review when Sander Berge was penalised for a handball in the box as he jumped with Leon Goretzka at a corner. With neither Emi Buendia nor Ross Barkley in the line-up, John McGinn stepped up to take the penalty but the Scotland international - who had only ever taken a penalty for Villa in a shoot-out - smashed the ball against the crossbar and over.

messages.text: Hamilton claims first pole for Ferrari at Mexico City GP

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton claimed his first pole position for Ferrari by edging out Mercedes' George Russell in qualifying for the Mexico City Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Mexico City GP Qualifying: Lewis Hamilton claims first pole position for Ferrari by edging out Mercedes' George Russell | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mexico City GP Qualifying: Lewis Hamilton claims first pole position for Ferrari by edging out Mercedes' George Russell Lewis Hamilton claims first grand prix pole position for Ferrari in Mexico City; Hamilton edged out George Russell for first pole since July 2023; watch Sunday's race at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm) to see if Kimi Antonelli can become champion, live on Sky Sports F1 Sunday 1 November 2026 01:33, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix. Lewis Hamilton claimed his first pole position for Ferrari by edging out Mercedes' George Russell in qualifying for the Mexico City Grand Prix. Hamilton had been outpaced by his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc throughout the weekend but the 41-year-old produced his best lap when it mattered most at the end of Q3 to edge out Russell by nine thousandths of a second. The seven-time world champion has twice claimed Sprint poles since his move from Mercedes to Ferrari at the start of the 2025 season but will now start a grand prix from the front of the grid for the first time since July 2023 after extending his record tally to 105 poles.
